note: Four unapproved beta2 agonists reached asthma patients on four different preclinical programs: abediterol and AZD3199 gave the once-daily bronchodilation their guinea-pig duration models predicted and were dropped without a Phase 3; carmoterol's guinea-pig duration claim failed at 2 ug once daily on 24-h trough FEV1; and intravenous bedoradrine, carried into acute asthma on a tocolytic-era rat organ-bath screen, missed its 3-h FEV1 primary in the emergency department.
label: Asthma (beta2 agonists)

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled). Guinea-pig acetylcholine bronchoprotection t1/2 36 h, human isolated bronchi EC50 1.9 nM with t1/2 ~690 min, and a dog safety margin of 5.6 (dose raising heart rate 5% over dose inhibiting bronchospasm 50%) are all in the abstract. Abediterol was never filed, so model_filed is null. The same model system is scored for COPD in the sibling tile.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry: the model existed and was used for a member drug before any asthma patient comparison was public. Aparici 2016 (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.ejphar.2015.11.053) later re-ran the same guinea-pig and dog models against indacaterol, olodaterol and vilanterol; same system, so no new track.
engagement.model: Almirall guinea-pig acetylcholine bronchoprotection, human isolated bronchi, and dog bronchoprotection-versus-heart-rate safety margin (abediterol)
engagement.note: Abediterol was picked on guinea-pig bronchoprotection (t1/2 36 h), human bronchi and a dog heart-rate margin; no asthma patient readout yet.
engagement.short: Guinea pig, human bronchi, dog picked abediterol
engagement.quote: In conclusion, our results suggest that abediterol has a preclinical profile for once-daily dosing in humans together with a fast onset of action and a favorable cardiovascular safety profile.

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled). First-in-patient five-way crossover (abediterol 5, 10, 25 ug, salmeterol, placebo; male persistent asthmatics on ICS); no ClinicalTrials.gov record was found for it, so registry_date is null. Healthy volunteers had already shown 36-h airway-conductance gains at 5-50 ug (Timmer 2014, https://doi.org/10.1002/jcph.355, online 2014-07-08). The dose-ranging study NCT01425801 (Singh 2014, https://doi.org/10.1186/1471-2466-14-176; results posted 2018-01-26) confirmed 24-h duration at 0.313-2.5 ug.
engagement.judgement: FEV1 over 36 h is the downstream readout of the same airway smooth-muscle relaxation the guinea-pig bronchoprotection and human-bronchus duration models measured; no occupancy measure exists for an inhaled LABA. Dated to the first asthma patient paper (online 2014-09-08).
engagement.model: Almirall guinea-pig acetylcholine bronchoprotection, human isolated bronchi, and dog bronchoprotection-versus-heart-rate safety margin (abediterol)
engagement.note: Single-dose abediterol 5-25 ug on top of ICS raised trough FEV1 over placebo and salmeterol in persistent asthma, with improvements sustained to 36 h: the duration the tissue models showed.
engagement.short: FEV1 up to 36 h in asthma patients
engagement.quote: These improvements were sustained to 36 h post-dose.

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled). Radioligand association/dissociation kinetics on human beta1- and beta2-adrenoceptors (tritiated abediterol; residence time 91-186 min, dissociation 30-64x slower than reference LABAs). Online 2017-11-26, print 2018. Built after the 2014 asthma and 2016 COPD patient data were public, so its only comparison is a retrodiction, entered next.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry at first public use. A different system from the tissue/animal duration models (receptor kinetics, not bronchoprotection), so its own track. model_kind is ex_vivo as the nearest enum for an in vitro human-receptor assay.
engagement.model: Almirall human beta2-adrenoceptor association-rate and residence-time assay (tritiated abediterol vs indacaterol, olodaterol, vilanterol, salmeterol)

engagement.quote: In conclusion, abediterol is a potent LABA with a fast association rate and a long residence time at β-adrenoceptors.

engagement.magnitude_basis: receptor residence time (91-186 min) vs onset and 24-36 h bronchodilation in humans; the paper reports agreement in direction, no fold error
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled). The human data it refers to are not named in the abstract; abediterol's asthma onset/duration results were public from 2014 (Beier 2014, Singh 2014).

engagement.judgement: Retrodiction (decision 10): the kinetic model was run after the human onset and duration were known and the paper states the agreement itself, so retro, never same. Class level; it made no prospective prediction for any member drug.
engagement.model: Almirall human beta2-adrenoceptor association-rate and residence-time assay (tritiated abediterol vs indacaterol, olodaterol, vilanterol, salmeterol)
engagement.note: Fast association and 30-64x slower dissociation than reference LABAs were set beside abediterol's known fast onset and 24-36 h duration in humans and found to agree.
engagement.short: Receptor kinetics refit known human duration
engagement.quote: These data are in agreement with the onset and duration of action of abediterol shown in humans.

engagement.confidence_note: Open access (PMC4027610), abstract-level reading. AZD3199 was in asthma patients from August 2008 (NCT00736489), so the model predates its 2014 publication (online 2014-02-08); 2014 is the earliest public record. Never filed, so model_filed is null. The same system is scored for COPD in the sibling tile.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry at the earliest public record of the model (2014); the compound was in Phase 2 by 2008.

engagement.note: AZD3199 was picked in guinea-pig histamine bronchoconstriction, tracheal/human bronchial ring onset and intratracheal duration models; no asthma patient readout paired yet.
engagement.quote: Determination of activities at the human β-adrenoreceptors demonstrated a series of highly potent and selective β2 receptor agonists that were progressed to further study in a guinea pig histamine-induced bronchoconstriction model.

engagement.magnitude_basis: duration: guinea-pig intratracheal duration vs 22-26 h FEV1 in patients; no FEV1 magnitude was predicted
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled). Single-dose six-way crossover in 37 asthmatics (AZD3199 120, 480, 1920 ug; formoterol 9, 36 ug; placebo), NCT00736489, results posted 2014-04-03. The 120 ug dose did not significantly raise 22-26 h FEV1.
engagement.judgement: The trial (online 2013-08-01) predates the model paper (online 2014-02-08), so the earliest public pairing is 2014 (rule 6); the model was run before the trial, so not a retrodiction. FEV1 at 22-26 h is the downstream readout of the relaxation the intratracheal duration model measured.
engagement.model: AstraZeneca guinea-pig histamine bronchoconstriction, tracheal and human bronchial ring onset, and intratracheal duration models (AZD3199)
engagement.note: Single doses of AZD3199 480 and 1920 ug held FEV1 over placebo at 22-26 h in 37 asthmatics, the 24-h airway relaxation the intratracheal duration model showed; 120 ug did not.
engagement.quote: AZD3199 480 µg and 1920 µg produced 24-hour bronchodilation.

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level; JPET 297:666-671 (PMID 11303056, no DOI on the PubMed record). Kissei built bedoradrine (KUR-1246) as a uterine relaxant: pregnant-rat uterus, atrium, trachea and colon in the organ bath, in vivo rat uterine motility, and human beta1/2/3 binding. Inoue 2009 (https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1447-0756.2008.01001.x) later gave the trachea EC50 as 1,610 nM against 1.01 nM for uterus. No MediciNova airway model was found in any peer-reviewed source; its press material names unpublished in vitro and in vivo selectivity work only.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry. The only published preclinical airway data for bedoradrine are this tocolytic-program organ-bath screen, in which rat trachea relaxed via beta2 but 1,590-fold less potently than uterus; it is the model the asthma program rested on in the public record. Different system and prediction from the inhaled-LABA duration models, so its own track.
engagement.model: Kissei pregnant-rat isolated uterus, atrium, trachea and colon organ-bath selectivity screen with in vivo rat uterine motility and human beta-adrenoceptor binding (bedoradrine / KUR-1246)
engagement.note: Bedoradrine was profiled as a beta2-selective uterine relaxant; rat trachea relaxed only at micromolar concentrations. No asthma patient readout yet.
engagement.short: Rat organ bath profiled bedoradrine as tocolytic
engagement.quote: The selectivity of KUR-1246 was assessed simultaneously in organs isolated from late-pregnant rats.

engagement.magnitude_basis: tracheal relaxation via beta2 (rat EC50 1.6 uM) vs dose- and plasma-concentration-related FEV1 rise in stable asthma; not the same quantity
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled). Two trials, n=40: MN-221-CL-004 dose escalation in stable mild-to-moderate asthma and MN-221-CL-005 (NCT00679263; results posted 2011-12-15) fixed dose over 1- or 2-h infusion in moderate-to-severe asthma. The registry posting for CL-005 precedes the paper (online 2012-10-25); a re-dater could set 2011.
engagement.reason: FEV1 rose with dose and plasma level
engagement.judgement: FEV1 is the downstream readout of the beta2-mediated tracheal relaxation the organ bath measured; intravenous dosing gives a plasma-concentration-response, the closest an asthma beta2 agonist comes to an exposure-engagement link. Dated to the paper that carries the quote.
engagement.model: Kissei pregnant-rat isolated uterus, atrium, trachea and colon organ-bath selectivity screen with in vivo rat uterine motility and human beta-adrenoceptor binding (bedoradrine / KUR-1246)
engagement.note: Intravenous bedoradrine raised FEV1 over placebo with a significant dose response in 40 stable asthmatics, plateauing at 30 ug/min: the beta2 airway relaxation the rat trachea showed.
engagement.short: IV dose-response on FEV1 in stable asthma
engagement.quote: Dose escalation results showed that mean changes in FEV₁ from pre-infusion were significantly greater than placebo and an overall dose response was statistically significant (p < .0001).

engagement.confidence_note: Open access (PMC1576020), abstract-level reading. Anaesthetised guinea pigs, intratracheal CHF 4226.01 against acetaldehyde-evoked airway obstruction: ED50 1.88-3.31 pmol vs formoterol 3.03-5.51 pmol, duration AUC 763 vs 480 at 10 pmol. Rossoni 2006 (https://doi.org/10.1016/j.pupt.2006.01.004) added acetylcholine, histamine and ovalbumin challenges in the same preparation. Carmoterol was never filed, so model_filed is null. Earlier TA-2005 tissue work (Voss 1992) was not verified within budget.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry at the first verified guinea-pig airway paper for carmoterol; the 2 ug once-daily asthma trials ran 2005-2007, so the model predates them. A Chiesi system distinct from the Almirall and AstraZeneca programs, so its own track.
engagement.model: Chiesi anaesthetised guinea-pig bronchoconstriction against acetaldehyde, acetylcholine, histamine and ovalbumin challenge with intratracheal dosing and duration-of-protection readout (carmoterol / CHF 4226)
engagement.note: Carmoterol out-ranked formoterol on potency and duration of bronchoprotection in anaesthetised guinea pigs; no asthma patient readout public yet.
engagement.short: Guinea pig: longer protection than formoterol
engagement.quote: The duration of action of CHF 4226.01 in antagonizing the airway obstruction elicited by AcCHO was also substantially longer than formoterol (area under the curve) at 10 pmol, 763+/-58 and 480+/-34, respectively; P<0.01).

engagement.magnitude_basis: bronchoprotection in guinea pig vs peak FEV1 +0.241 L over placebo at week 4; the model gave no FEV1 magnitude
engagement.confidence_note: EU Clinical Trials Register results record (EudraCT 2006-005689-38; Chiesi clinical study report CCD-0604-RS-0009, ICH E3 synopsis read in full). 252 moderate-to-severe asthmatics on ICS, 4 weeks, CHF 4226 2 ug once daily in the evening vs formoterol 12 ug twice daily vs placebo; trial ended 2007-07-18, results posted 2017-01-01. Conference abstracts from 2006-2008 are not admissible, so the comparison is dated to the registry posting.
engagement.reason: Peak FEV1 moved; 24-h trough did not
engagement.judgement: The downstream airway readout moved (peak FEV1 and FEV1 AUC 0-3 h both p<0.001 vs placebo at every visit), so engagement is same; the duration claim is scored under dose and efficacy. The 7-day trial (EudraCT 2005-002195-15) synopsis could not be downloaded.
engagement.model: Chiesi anaesthetised guinea-pig bronchoconstriction against acetaldehyde, acetylcholine, histamine and ovalbumin challenge with intratracheal dosing and duration-of-protection readout (carmoterol / CHF 4226)
engagement.note: Carmoterol 2 ug once daily raised peak FEV1 by 0.241 L and FEV1 AUC 0-3 h by 0.222 L over placebo (both p<0.001) after 4 weeks in 252 asthmatics: the beta2 bronchodilation the guinea pig showed.
engagement.quote: The LS mean treatment difference between CHF 4226 and placebo for peak FEV1 after 4 weeks of treatment was 0.241 L (p <0.001 ) and for FEV1 AUC(0,3) was 0.222 L (p <0.001).

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled); J Biomech 41:106-113, online 2007-08-14, print January 2008. The abstract names only 'a novel long acting beta2 agonist (LABA) that acts shortly after inhalation'; carmoterol is identified from the record's indexed substances (MeSH: carmoterol). 14 mild-to-moderately severe asthmatics: 10 scanned before and 4 h after the dose, 4 scanned twice after bronchodilator wash-out as controls. No registry record found for this 2007 imaging study.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry at first public use. Not an animal: an in-silico airflow model solved on each patient's own CT geometry, so model_kind in_silico, its own track. The comparison with spirometry is in the same paper and follows as the next entry.
engagement.model: Antwerp patient-specific computational fluid dynamics of HRCT airway geometries reading regional airway resistance 4 h after a single inhaled dose of carmoterol in asthmatics
engagement.note: Patient-specific CFD on HRCT airway geometries, built to read regional airway resistance change after a single inhaled dose of carmoterol in 14 asthmatics.
engagement.short: Patient-CT CFD model built around carmoterol
engagement.quote: The aim of the present study was to improve the actual imaging techniques by subsequent analysis of the imaging data using computational fluid dynamics (CFD).

engagement.magnitude_basis: CFD total and distal airway resistance change vs FEV1 change 4 h after carmoterol in 10 asthmatics: r = -0.73 and -0.76, distal airway volume r = 0.69; a correlation, no fold error to compute
engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled). Active group FEV1 +8.78 +/- 6.27 % predicted vs -3.38 +/- 6.87 in controls. The source states the agreement itself (comparison_stated). Drug identity rests on the indexed substance list, not the abstract text; no registry record found.
engagement.reason: CFD resistance tracked FEV1 after carmoterol
engagement.judgement: Same on engagement: the model's own readout, regional airway resistance computed from the patient's CT, moved in dosed asthmatics and the paper states its agreement with spirometry. It is a concurrent readout validation in one experiment, not a prediction made before the patient result, so no retrodiction flag; it does not pick patients, so class level. A re-scorer who wants a model to precede its patient result may set this aside.
engagement.model: Antwerp patient-specific computational fluid dynamics of HRCT airway geometries reading regional airway resistance 4 h after a single inhaled dose of carmoterol in asthmatics
engagement.note: In 10 asthmatics FEV1 rose 8.8% predicted 4 h after carmoterol and CFD-computed total and distal airway resistance fell in step (r = -0.73, -0.76).
engagement.short: CFD airway resistance fell with FEV1
engagement.quote: All changes in the CFD-based calculated R(aw) significantly correlate with the observed changes in spirometric values therefore validating the CFD method for the studied application.

engagement.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled); Eur J Pharmacol 227:403-409, December 1992, DOI verified on Europe PMC. pD2 9.29 vs 7.65 isoprenaline and 7.10 salbutamol; one binding state (pKd 8.2) without GppNHp. Sykes 2012 (https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1476-5381.2011.01639.x, PMC3423252, full text read) later measured carmoterol koff 0.46 min-1 (t1/2 1.5 min) in CHO-beta2 membranes with GTP and wrote that its washout duration 'is more likely to be attributable to membrane interactions and so-called drug rebinding': the mechanism was not reproduced in vitro, but that is a model-against-model test, not a patient comparison, so it changes no status.
engagement.judgement: Opening entry. A receptor-binding system, not the guinea-pig bronchoconstriction model: like the Almirall kinetics track it predicts duration from the drug-receptor interaction, so its own track. The Tanabe in vivo and organ-bath airway papers (Kikkawa 1991, Kikkawa 1994) are the same system as the Chiesi guinea-pig track and are not re-opened here.
engagement.model: Tanabe-era in vitro receptor-binding kinetics of TA-2005 (carmoterol): methacholine-precontracted guinea-pig trachea relaxation with bovine trapezium beta2 binding and GppNHp shift, tight binding offered as the basis of a long duration of action
engagement.note: Guinea-pig trachea relaxation (pD2 9.29) and bovine trapezium binding: one tight-binding state without GppNHp, offered as the basis of a long duration of action.
engagement.short: Tight binding predicted long duration for carmoterol
engagement.quote: The long duration of action of TA 2005 might be explained by tight binding of this compound to the beta 2-adrenoceptor.

engagement.magnitude_basis: tracheal relaxation pD2 9.29 and tight binding vs peak FEV1 +0.241 L over placebo at week 4; the model gave no FEV1 magnitude
engagement.confidence_note: EU Clinical Trials Register results record (EudraCT 2006-005689-38; Chiesi CSR CCD-0604-RS-0009 synopsis), the same record and quote the draft's Chiesi-track engagement entry carries (read in full by the drafter, verified by the checker; not re-downloaded here). 252 moderate-to-severe asthmatics on ICS, CHF 4226 2 ug once daily vs formoterol 12 ug twice daily vs placebo for 4 weeks; results posted 2017-01-01. Conference abstracts from 2006-2008 are not admissible.
engagement.judgement: The downstream readout moved (peak FEV1 and FEV1 AUC 0-3 h p<0.001 vs placebo), so same on engagement, as on the Chiesi track; the duration claim is scored under efficacy. Dated to the registry posting. By then Sykes 2012 had shown the tight-binding mechanism does not hold in vitro, so the bronchodilation prediction was right for a reason the model got wrong.
engagement.model: Tanabe-era in vitro receptor-binding kinetics of TA-2005 (carmoterol): methacholine-precontracted guinea-pig trachea relaxation with bovine trapezium beta2 binding and GppNHp shift, tight binding offered as the basis of a long duration of action
engagement.note: Carmoterol 2 ug once daily raised peak FEV1 0.241 L over placebo at week 4: the bronchodilation the binding assay implied; 24-h trough did not.
engagement.short: Peak FEV1 up, as tight binding implied
engagement.quote: The LS mean treatment difference between CHF 4226 and placebo for peak FEV1 after 4 weeks of treatment was 0.241 L (p <0.001 ) and for FEV1 AUC(0,3) was 0.222 L (p <0.001).

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled). Guinea-pig bronchoprotection t1/2 36 h, human bronchi t1/2 ~690 min and a dog margin of 5.6 are in the abstract; no human dose was derived.
dose.model: Almirall guinea-pig acetylcholine bronchoprotection, human isolated bronchi, and dog bronchoprotection-versus-heart-rate safety margin (abediterol)

dose.short: Dog set 5.6x margin and once daily
dose.quote: In conclusion, our results suggest that abediterol has a preclinical profile for once-daily dosing in humans together with a fast onset of action and a favorable cardiovascular safety profile.

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled). Single doses 5-25 ug; adrenergic adverse events only at 10 and 25 ug. Singh 2014 (NCT01425801, results 2018-01-26) then found 0.625-2.5 ug effective over 24 h with no clinically relevant heart-rate change, and Beier 2017 (EudraCT 2008-003732-38, https://doi.org/10.1002/prp2.356) 2.5-10 ug once daily for 7 days with placebo-like tolerability.
dose.reason: Once daily and dog margin held in patients
dose.judgement: Decision 16: the dog stated that bronchoprotective doses were free of heart-rate effects (margin 5.6); asthma patients were dosed to every effective dose (0.313-25 ug) with systemic adrenergic effects confined to the top doses, so margin_stated is true and dose is same. The once-daily aim held at 24-36 h. The program's end without a Phase 3 is not a dose failure and no reason was found in the sources used.
dose.model: Almirall guinea-pig acetylcholine bronchoprotection, human isolated bronchi, and dog bronchoprotection-versus-heart-rate safety margin (abediterol)
dose.note: Once-daily target reached and sufficient: 5 ug held trough FEV1 at 24 h with no related adverse events; adrenergic effects appeared only at 10-25 ug, inside the dog margin.
dose.quote: The profile of treatment-emergent adverse events judged as related to abediterol was consistent with that seen after adrenergic stimulation and occurred exclusively in patients who received abediterol 10 μg or 25 μg.

dose.confidence_note: Open access (PMC4027610), abstract-level reading. The model predates its 2014 publication (asthma trial from 2008).
dose.model: AstraZeneca guinea-pig histamine bronchoconstriction, tracheal and human bronchial ring onset, and intratracheal duration models (AZD3199)
dose.note: Guinea-pig intratracheal duration set a once-daily aim for AZD3199; no human dose was derived from it.
dose.short: Guinea pig set once-daily aim, no dose
dose.quote: Determination of activities at the human β-adrenoreceptors demonstrated a series of highly potent and selective β2 receptor agonists that were progressed to further study in a guinea pig histamine-induced bronchoconstriction model.

dose.magnitude_basis: 24-h dosing interval; the model gave no human dose
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled). NCT00736489 (results 2014-04-03). Relative dose potency vs formoterol was 50-fold on peak and 11-fold on 22-26 h FEV1. The later asthma formulation study NCT01348139 (results 2013-03-05) and the COPD Phase 2b did not change the regimen; no Phase 3 was registered and no reason was published.
dose.judgement: The model claimed once-daily potential; 480 and 1920 ug held FEV1 at 22-26 h after a single dose, so the regimen target was reached and sufficient, while 120 ug fell short, which sets the floor rather than contradicting the model. No tolerated-dose margin was stated by the guinea-pig model, so margin_stated is false.
dose.model: AstraZeneca guinea-pig histamine bronchoconstriction, tracheal and human bronchial ring onset, and intratracheal duration models (AZD3199)
dose.note: Once-daily target reached: single 480 and 1920 ug doses held FEV1 at 22-26 h over placebo; 120 ug did not. Dose set by clinical ranging, not by the model.
dose.short: Once daily reached at 480 ug, not 120
dose.quote: All active treatments dose-dependently increased E(max) and AZD3199 (480 and 1920 µg) and formoterol (36 µg) significantly increased E(₂₂₋₂₆) versus placebo.

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level; PMID 11303056, no DOI. In vivo rat uterine ED30 0.13 ug/kg/min was the only exposure figure; no airway dose or human exposure was derived.
dose.model: Kissei pregnant-rat isolated uterus, atrium, trachea and colon organ-bath selectivity screen with in vivo rat uterine motility and human beta-adrenoceptor binding (bedoradrine / KUR-1246)
dose.note: The rat screen gave a tocolytic ED30 and a tracheal EC50 in the micromolar range; no airway exposure target or human dose was derived.
dose.short: Rat screen set no airway dose
dose.quote: The selectivity of KUR-1246 was assessed simultaneously in organs isolated from late-pregnant rats.

dose.magnitude_basis: bronchodilating exposure reached (FEV1 plateau at 30 ug/min); the model gave no human target to compare
dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled). n=40 across CL-004 and CL-005 (NCT00679263; results 2011-12-15). Plasma concentrations were linear with dose; FEV1 gains plateaued at 30 ug/min despite higher Cmax at 60 ug/min.
dose.judgement: Reached, drug worked: intravenous infusion gave a plasma-concentration-related FEV1 rise with a plateau, so a bronchodilating exposure was found in stable asthma. The model set no exposure target, so this is a regimen match only.
dose.model: Kissei pregnant-rat isolated uterus, atrium, trachea and colon organ-bath selectivity screen with in vivo rat uterine motility and human beta-adrenoceptor binding (bedoradrine / KUR-1246)
dose.note: A bronchodilating intravenous exposure was reached in stable asthma: FEV1 rose with dose and plasma level and plateaued at 30 ug/min, the rate later carried into the exacerbation trial as 1200 ug over 1 h.
dose.quote: Post-infusion FEV1 improvements appeared to plateau at the 30 μg/min dose level despite a higher peak plasma concentration at 60 μg/min.

dose.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled). MN-221-CL-007 (NCT00838591; 167 randomised, no registry results posted). 1200 ug over 1 h, the exposure that bronchodilated stable asthmatics, was given on top of 5-15 mg nebulised albuterol, ipratropium and a systemic steroid. No further bedoradrine asthma trial was registered after 2012.
dose.reason: Exposure reached; primary failed; no further trial
dose.judgement: Reached, failed, abandoned: the bronchodilating exposure found in 2012 was delivered in the emergency department and the 3-h FEV1 primary missed, so dose is contra derived from efficacy (counted once). The toxic end was never reached (no blocked_by). A re-scorer could argue the failure was a ceiling from prior nebulised beta2 agonist, not a dose miss; that reading would leave dose same and efficacy untested.
dose.model: Kissei pregnant-rat isolated uterus, atrium, trachea and colon organ-bath selectivity screen with in vivo rat uterine motility and human beta-adrenoceptor binding (bedoradrine / KUR-1246)
dose.note: The bronchodilating exposure (1200 ug IV over 1 h) was given to 167 acute-exacerbation patients on top of standard therapy and the 3-h FEV1 primary missed; no further trial followed.
dose.quote: Intravenous bedoradrine, in addition to standard therapy, did not significantly increase %FEV1 at 3 h, but it was associated with significantly improved dyspnea scores.

dose.confidence_note: Open access (PMC1576020), abstract-level reading. Intratracheal picomole doses in guinea pigs; duration expressed as AUC of protection. No human dose was derived.
dose.model: Chiesi anaesthetised guinea-pig bronchoconstriction against acetaldehyde, acetylcholine, histamine and ovalbumin challenge with intratracheal dosing and duration-of-protection readout (carmoterol / CHF 4226)

dose.quote: The duration of action of CHF 4226.01 in antagonizing the airway obstruction elicited by AcCHO was also substantially longer than formoterol (area under the curve) at 10 pmol, 763+/-58 and 480+/-34, respectively; P<0.01).

dose.confidence_note: EU CTR synopsis (EudraCT 2006-005689-38) read in full. Trough FEV1 LS mean difference vs placebo 0.057 L (not significant) against 0.157 L for formoterol 12 ug twice daily. A higher carmoterol dose (4 ug once daily) was later tested only inside the budesonide/carmoterol combination CHF 5188 (NCT01070524, 2010; EudraCT 2008-001773-15), whose synopsis could not be downloaded, so the 'higher dose later worked' branch could not be checked; no monotherapy trial followed.
dose.reason: Once-daily regimen failed at 2 ug; dropped
dose.judgement: Reached, failed, abandoned: the regimen the guinea pig implied (once daily, longer than formoterol) was tested at 2 ug and did not hold trough FEV1 at 24 h while twice-daily formoterol did, and no further carmoterol monotherapy trial followed. Scored contra derived from efficacy so the one failure counts once. If the combination synopsis shows 4 ug holding trough FEV1, this becomes 'target too low' with the same status.
dose.model: Chiesi anaesthetised guinea-pig bronchoconstriction against acetaldehyde, acetylcholine, histamine and ovalbumin challenge with intratracheal dosing and duration-of-protection readout (carmoterol / CHF 4226)

patient_trials.quote: All three abediterol doses induced statistically significant increases in trough FEV1 vs placebo and salmeterol.

efficacy.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled). MN-221-CL-007 (NCT00838591; 167 randomised; 1200 ug IV as adjunct to nebulised albuterol, ipratropium and systemic steroid; FEV1 <=50% predicted at entry; no registry results posted). Dyspnoea secondary improved (AUC 0-2 h p<0.005). Earlier, Cochrane (Travers 2012, https://doi.org/10.1002/14651858.CD010179, tier 4) found no significant hospitalisation advantage for IV bedoradrine in a 29-adult conference-abstract trial (Nowak 2010; NCT00683449, terminated).
efficacy.reason: 3-h FEV1 primary missed on top of albuterol
efficacy.judgement: Scored contra on the primary endpoint: the model predicted beta2 bronchodilation and the pre-specified 3-h %FEV1 did not move in patients already treated with high-dose nebulised beta2 agonist. Caveats a re-scorer could act on: the model was a tocolytic organ-bath screen with no exacerbation or beta2-refractory component, so 'untested' is defensible; the secondary dyspnoea endpoint improved. Dated to the paper (online 2015-08-14); the trial completed 2012-03 and its result was first released in a 2012 sponsor press release not used here.

efficacy.magnitude_basis: duration: guinea-pig protection AUC 763 vs 480 for formoterol at 10 pmol, against trough FEV1 +0.057 L (NS) for carmoterol 2 ug once daily vs +0.157 L for formoterol twice daily; the predicted rank reversed
efficacy.confidence_note: EU CTR synopsis (EudraCT 2006-005689-38; CSR CCD-0604-RS-0009 dated 2010-03-02) read in full; 252 randomised, 243 completed; trial ended 2007-07-18, results posted 2017-01-01. Secondary peak FEV1, FEV1 AUC 0-3 h and morning PEF favoured carmoterol; symptom and rescue-use outcomes did not separate for either active arm. The 7-day trial (EudraCT 2005-002195-15, trough FEV1 Day 8 primary, results posted 2017-01-01) synopsis could not be downloaded. Conference abstracts from 2006-2008 may have made the result public earlier but are not admissible.
efficacy.reason: Guinea pig said longer than formoterol; patients said shorter
efficacy.judgement: Contra: the model's one testable claim, protection lasting longer than formoterol, was tested as 2 ug once daily against formoterol 12 ug twice daily and the primary trough FEV1 at 24 h did not beat placebo while formoterol's did. The sponsor's own synopsis notes earlier 24-h bronchodilation data (not public in an admissible form). A re-scorer might treat it as a dose-selection miss rather than a model miss; under the dose table both cells carry one contra. The combination program (CHF 5188, carmoterol 4 ug) ran in 2010 and was not followed by a Phase 3.

Healthy volunteers (Timmer 2014) had shown dose-dependent mild palpitations and tremor at 5-50 ug; Singh 2014 (NCT01425801) found no clinically relevant heart-rate change at 0.313-2.5 ug; Beier 2017 found 7-day tolerability comparable with placebo at 2.5-10 ug.

safety.judgement: The model predicted class-related cardiac effects at a multiple of the effective dose, not their absence; adrenergic adverse events confined to the 10-25 ug arms while 5 ug bronchodilated match that in direction. Single-dose and 7-day exposure only, so nothing on chronic cardiac effects.
safety.model: Almirall guinea-pig acetylcholine bronchoprotection, human isolated bronchi, and dog bronchoprotection-versus-heart-rate safety margin (abediterol)

safety.quote: The profile of treatment-emergent adverse events judged as related to abediterol was consistent with that seen after adrenergic stimulation and occurred exclusively in patients who received abediterol 10 μg or 25 μg.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled). Conscious dogs: no blood-pressure, heart-rate or femoral-flow effect at 0.1-1 ug/kg IV, blood pressure down and heart rate up at 10-100 ug/kg, no QT/QTc change; no effect on guinea-pig papillary action potentials or hERG tail current at 10 uM. A tocolytic-program safety study; the same drug and route as the asthma program.
safety.judgement: Opening entry. A different system and prediction from the organ-bath screen (cardiovascular telemetry and hERG vs tissue relaxation), so its own track. The stated prediction: beta2 class haemodynamic effects only at high dose, and no ventricular repolarisation risk.
safety.model: Kissei conscious-dog intravenous cardiovascular telemetry with guinea-pig papillary-muscle action potential and hERG assays (bedoradrine / KUR-1246)
safety.note: Conscious dogs predicted heart-rate and blood-pressure effects only at 10-100 ug/kg IV and no QT prolongation; hERG was clean.
safety.short: Dog: tachycardia at high dose, no QT
safety.quote: KUR-1246 at 10 and 100 microg/kg significantly decreased blood pressure and increased heart rate.

safety.magnitude_basis: heart-rate rise: dog only at 10-100 ug/kg IV vs a mild dose-related rise in patients at infusion rates up to 60 ug/min; routes and doses not comparable
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled). n=40 stable asthmatics (CL-004, CL-005/NCT00679263; results 2011-12-15); ECGs were monitored and no dose-dependent effect beyond heart rate is reported. House 2015 (167 exacerbation patients at 1200 ug) likewise reports cardiovascular and metabolic effects consistent with beta2 agonism. Hypokalaemia (seen in patients) was a stated finding of the sheep infusion studies (Kiguchi 2002), not of the dog.
safety.reason: High-dose tachycardia, no QT, as dog predicted
safety.judgement: The dog predicted a heart-rate rise at high dose and no repolarisation effect; patients showed a mild dose-related heart-rate rise not needing treatment and no reported ECG signal, matching in direction. Dated to the paper carrying the quote (online 2012-10-25); the registry posting for CL-005 was earlier (2011-12-15).
safety.model: Kissei conscious-dog intravenous cardiovascular telemetry with guinea-pig papillary-muscle action potential and hERG assays (bedoradrine / KUR-1246)
safety.note: Held: in 40 stable asthmatics the only dose-dependent safety signal was a clinically insignificant heart-rate rise; tremor, hypokalaemia and headache were the common events and no ECG signal was reported.
safety.short: Only heart rate moved, mildly, as predicted
safety.quote: There were no consistent dose-dependent effects of MN-221 on any safety parameters, with the exception of heart rate, which was not considered to be clinically significant and did not require any treatment.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level; JPET 271:386-389 (PMID 7965739, no DOI on the PubMed record). TA 2005 is carmoterol's original Tanabe code. Guinea-pig right atrium: biphasic chronotropic response reaching 84% of isoprenaline, ~64% via beta2; the paper proposes the tissue as a model for clinical cardiac side effects.
safety.judgement: Opening entry. An academic isolated-heart system eleven years before the Chiesi airway model and a different prediction (on-target beta2 tachycardia), so its own track.
safety.model: Guinea-pig isolated right atrium, left atrium and papillary muscle chronotropic/inotropic assay proposed as a model of clinical cardiac side effects (carmoterol / TA 2005)
safety.note: Guinea-pig atria predicted that carmoterol would raise heart rate partly through beta2 itself (64% of its chronotropic response), so selectivity would not abolish tachycardia.
safety.quote: Approximately 64% of the TA 2005 chronotropic response was exerted via the beta-2 adrenoceptor.

safety.magnitude_basis: tachycardia: predicted as a beta2-mediated class effect; observed as an adverse event in 3.6% of carmoterol vs 1.2% of placebo patients with no substantial mean heart-rate rise
safety.confidence_note: EU CTR synopsis (EudraCT 2006-005689-38) read in full; 83 patients on carmoterol 2 ug for 4 weeks. Tachycardia 3/83 carmoterol, 3/84 formoterol, 1/85 placebo; no QTc effect; one sudden death on formoterol. Low confidence: the model proposed a mechanism, not a dose or incidence, and the patient signal is three adverse-event reports.
safety.reason: Tachycardia present, small, as atria predicted
safety.judgement: Same in direction: the atria said a selective beta2 agonist would still raise heart rate and tachycardia was the carmoterol-specific adverse event, at the same rate as formoterol; a re-scorer could call this untested because the model gave no quantitative prediction.
safety.model: Guinea-pig isolated right atrium, left atrium and papillary muscle chronotropic/inotropic assay proposed as a model of clinical cardiac side effects (carmoterol / TA 2005)
safety.note: Held in direction: tachycardia was reported in 3.6% of carmoterol and 1.2% of placebo patients over 4 weeks, with no substantial mean heart-rate rise and no QTc effect.
safety.quote: A small proportion of patients experienced tachycardia and palpitations in both active treatment groups as well as in the placebo group although no substantial increases in heart rate were observed in any treatment group.

safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled); Obstet Gynecol 100:487-494, print September 2002, no separate epub. Quote as rendered on PubMed/Europe PMC ('microg', 'K(+)'); the print text uses the micro sign and a superscript plus. Eight ewes at 123-125 days, oxytocin-driven contractions, KUR-1246 stepped 0.001 to 0.3 ug/kg/min over 3 h vs saline. The 24-h infusion at 0.03 ug/kg/min (Murata 2005 BJOG, https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1471-0528.2004.00333.x, PMID 15663400, the paper the checker calls Kanayama 2005) moved maternal heart rate, lactate, glucose and insulin but not electrolytes significantly and called the changes 'within the compensatory capacity'.
safety.judgement: Opening entry. A different system from the Kissei conscious-dog telemetry (Furihata 2006) and the rat organ bath: chronically instrumented pregnant ewes under stepwise intravenous infusion with electrolytes, lactate, glucose and insulin read, the one bedoradrine model that stated the metabolic harms. Safety only: its PD readout is uterine contraction, not an airway, and it set no airway exposure or margin.
safety.model: Kissei chronically instrumented pregnant-sheep intravenous infusion model of KUR-1246 (bedoradrine) tocolysis reading maternal and fetal heart rate, blood pressure, electrolytes, lactate, glucose and insulin
safety.note: Pregnant ewes infused stepwise to 0.3 ug/kg/min: above 0.03 heart rate, blood pressure, blood K+, lactate, glucose and insulin shifted; fewer such effects than ritodrine.
safety.short: Sheep predicted hypokalaemia, tachycardia at tocolytic doses
safety.quote: Significant differences between the two groups were found at high doses over 0.03 microg/kg/minute for the following parameters: maternal heart rate, diastolic blood pressure, mean blood pressure, base excess, blood K(+), blood lactate, plasma glucose, plasma insulin

safety.magnitude_basis: hypokalaemia and heart rate: sheep blood K+ and heart rate shifted above 0.03 ug/kg/min IV at tocolytic exposure; asthmatics at 3-60 ug/min IV had hypokalaemia as the second commonest AE (moderate in 2 of 40) and a mild dose-related heart-rate rise; species, doses and infusion regimens not comparable
safety.confidence_note: Abstract-level (paywalled). n=40 stable asthmatics (MN-221-CL-004 dose escalation 3-60 ug/min; CL-005 fixed dose over 1 or 2 h, NCT00679263, results posted 2011-12-15). The registry AE table lists 'Hyperkalemia' 2/11 and 4/11 on MN-221 vs 1/6 placebo, the opposite direction to the paper's hypokalaemia that needed oral KCl, so the registry posting does not carry the comparison and the entry is dated to the paper (online 2012-10-25). House 2015 (n=167, 1200 ug in exacerbations) reports cardiovascular and metabolic effects consistent with beta2 agonism, no status change. Sheep blood lactate and glucose shifts have no bedoradrine patient record (Liedtke 2019 lists no bedoradrine).
safety.reason: Sheep hypokalaemia and tachycardia held in patients
safety.judgement: The sheep stated the harms (blood K+, heart rate, glucose, lactate) above the tocolytic dose, and hypokalaemia and a heart-rate rise both appeared in asthmatics at bronchodilating infusion rates: a direction match, made prospectively (2002, before any asthma trial), so same not retro. Counted here and not in dose because the sheep set no airway exposure or margin (decision 16). The model ran in another indication but the patient side is asthma, so nothing is imported.
safety.model: Kissei chronically instrumented pregnant-sheep intravenous infusion model of KUR-1246 (bedoradrine) tocolysis reading maternal and fetal heart rate, blood pressure, electrolytes, lactate, glucose and insulin
safety.note: Held: in 40 asthmatics hypokalaemia was the second commonest AE, moderate in two subjects and reversed with oral KCl, with a mild dose-related heart-rate rise.
safety.short: Hypokalaemia and tachycardia held in asthma patients
safety.quote: The most frequently reported AEs were tremor, hypokalemia, and headache.
